This paper, as a critical component of an ongoing research for military aviation organisations, proposes a quality improvement method for the reduction of variability that exists in safety processes and other organisational issues of a system that has an impact on human factors performance. The overall thesis requirement is a revised, more comprehensive military pilot's error framework. The intent is to start to bridge and compare existent Flight Safety programmes among NATO/EU Air Forces and show how a tailored Safety Management System can be realised. This paper's outcome documents meaningful recommendations for military operators to further improve flight safety in combat training, by equipping them with a standard template for measuring their pilots' safety performance and their progress towards performance excellence. However, the methodology is based on a hypothetical but also “reasonable” example.

articleTitle: An extended quantitative risk analysis model by incorporating human and organizational factors
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: In this paper, a quantitative risk analysis (QRA) model incorporating human and organizational factor is presented by integrating Fault Tree (FT) with Bayesian Network (BN). FT is used to model the factors how to contribute to the final failures. BN extends the causal chain of basic events to potential human and organizational roots and provides a more precise quantitative links between the event nodes. In order to define the conditional probability table of BN, fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) is integrated with a decomposition method. The fuzzy AHP helps to reduce the subjective biases by avoiding the need to spell out explicit probability values for the variables' states. The decomposition method breaks the complexity by allowing conditioning on each of the parent nodes separately. The new QRA model is demonstrated on an offshore fire case study. By exploiting the advantages of both models, the method of combining FT and BN is normally a more detailed risk model with higher resolution, comparing with traditional QRA.

articleTitle: Six sigma approach for the reduction of transportation costs of a pipe manufacturing company
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Logistics is among the most important three businesses that will be improved in 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century together with information technology and micro biology. Logistics is efficiently planning, implementing and controlling materials in the supply chain, services and information flow. In the future, competition of companies won't be about products which they produce or about countries where these products are consumed, but it will be about the supply chains they use. Competition of companies will be raised by improving logistics processes. To reduce transportation that do not add value to the products and to deliver the products to customers in a short time will lead to reduce logistics' costs and in addition they will raise customers' satisfaction. Therefore, companies should optimize their logistics processes. This paper deals with the reduction of transportation costs of a pipe manufacturing company. For this purpose, the six sigma approach is utilized and its results are analyzed.

articleTitle: Estimating telecommunication equipment failures due to lightning surges by using population density
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Lightning damage to telecommunication infrastructures will become more serious with global warming because of the increased occurrence of lightning. To estimate the lightning damage to telecommunication equipment in the medium and long term, we have developed an estimation model that uses resident population, which we can calculate from highly reliable predicted demographic shifts in the future. We applied our model to three areas with different resident population densities by using statistical data on lightning strikes and resident population. The results demonstrated that our model could accurately estimate lightning damage in all the areas.

articleTitle: Fatal accidents in the construction sector — A Portuguese study
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The Construction Sector in Portugal shows high numbers of fatal accidents, with special occurrences in falls from height, crushing, burying and electrocution: From the 115 accidents in 2009, 56 came from this sector (ACT, 2009). So, it is important to understand better these matters bearing in mind what can be improved to minimize those numbers, namely what continues not to work properly and adequately. In this way, a research study was designed aiming to know and to analyze the content of the official reports related to fatal accidents. The Authority for Working Conditions (ACT) is the national body responsible for inspections and regulations in this field. Small and medium companies (SME) are the critical organizations, where safety procedures are not in place, nor legal regulations respected. The sequence of events was identified leading to fatal accidents.

articleTitle: Improve supply chain efficiency through a web-based system: A case study on a pharmaceutical company in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The supply chain operations in pharmaceutical industry are one of the most complex operations to manage. To efficiently manage the supply chain in this industry, information technology (IT) plays the crucial role. Over the last few decades, Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) has been employed in the pharmaceutical industry to synchronize information between business partners. However, an information standard is also needed to seamlessly exchange electronic documents between business partners. XML-based information technology is a promising tool and is starting to gain popularity over EDI-based technology. In this research, we study a medium size multinational pharmaceutical company in Thailand, and how a web-based system and a business standard for information flow (RosettaNet standard in this case) can be applied to improve efficiency in its supply chain operations. In particular, we examine the information flow during the process of order transactions between the pharmaceutical company, its customers (hospitals), and its distributors. We first examine the current business process and propose a new process with a web-based system. The new system is examined and the result is analyzed.

articleTitle: Towards a human reliability assessment in process model development: An empirical investigation on routing elements
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Process models provide a sound basis for quality management systems (QMS). Inconsistencies between process models and corporate reality are a common phenomenon in corporate practice. Erroneous routing is a major source for these inconsistencies that might hinder process implementation and maintenance as well as continuous improvement efforts. The approach presented in this paper accounts for a more active participation of employees in order to further increase the economical benefit of QMS. To this purpose, a human performance analysis in process model development with regard to routing elements was conducted. The results derived from data of 64 subjects show that omission and erroneous execution of routing elements is considerably higher for novices than for subjects with theoretical knowledge and experienced modelers. However, routing elements like the split and join or an embedded iteration are prone to reasoning fallacies and possible sources for inconsistencies.

articleTitle: The scale of tourism's economic, socio-cultural and environmental effects on local people: Developing scale, reliability and validity study
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Tourism is an economic, social and environmental phenomenon concerning of all the countries in the world. Tourism has been begun to be researched comprehensively regarding the revenue it provided and the cost it created. Tourism also affects the economic, social, cultural and environmental structure of the region in which tourism mobility takes place. A questionnaire developed through the evaluation of articles and thesis was used to collect the data. The questionnaire consists of four parts. The first part has 34 questions which are about the socio-cultural effects of tourism, second part has 9 questions which are about the environmental effects of tourism, the third part has 9 questions which are about the economic effects of tourism. The fourth part has questions about the demographic features of the participants. Researchers have reached 422 people who are living in Antalya with the polls he applied in November-December 2010.

articleTitle: An eigenvalue control charting for process variability monitoring
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper proposes a control charting of each eigenvalue of sample covariance matrix to monitor the shift in multivariate process variability. Its performance will be compared with sample generalized variance chart, the most widely used control charting in practice. A case study using a real industrial problem shows that both charts are complementary. They might give different signal.

articleTitle: A circle chart for periodic measurements
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Periodic measurements are very common in practice, with a specific characteristic, periodicity. In this paper, we propose a type of control chart that plots the measurement around a circle. By doing so, information from the same stage of different cycles can be compared easily. Some basic properties are investigated and further developments are discussed. The basic circle chart can also be applied under various kinds of control chart schemes. Furthermore, the circle chart has good chart performance and potential for further development. Application examples are also shown in this paper.

articleTitle: A high breakdown point robust Phase I operation of process variability monitoring based on individual observations
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper presents an improvement of data concentration process in FMCD algorithm in order to increase its computational efficiency. A simulation study indicates that the improved algorithm is promising in reducing the running time. This advantage will allow the users to use more efficiently that algorithm in multivariate analysis including in the development of a high breakdown point robust Phase I operation in monitoring manufacturing process quality based on individual observations. A real example in Phase I operation of process variability will be presented and discussed to illustrate the advantage of the proposed improved algorithm.

articleTitle: Quality assurance and risk management in Canadian police services: Theory and practice
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Quality assurance in the public sector presents interesting challenges and nowhere are these more obvious than in policing. While there was a high level of consensus around the aims of quality assurance in policing, this study of Canadian police services shows little consistency in approaches. A structured survey and open-ended interviews and surveys with management of law enforcement agencies, revealed a wide range of definitions, structures and tools. There was also a range of approaches to quality assurance, ranging from highly prescriptive compliance based approaches, which appear to have evolved from quality control and auditing functions through more process oriented approaches aligned with continuous improvement.

articleTitle: Uncertain quality abnormity diagnosis by stateflow-based simulating of Fuzzy Reasoning Petri Nets Model: A case study
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Fuzzy Reasoning Petri Nets (FRPNs) has been used widely to deal with fuzzy uncertain information in fault diagnosis. But for its particular graphic representation and logic structure, it is hard to simulate and analyze the process of abnormity producing and spreading dynamically. In this study, a stateflow-based method has been investigated for simulating FRPNs Model of uncertain quality abnormity diagnosis. In this method, elements of stateflow diagram, such as state, transition, state action and marking label of transition, are used to represent the place, directed arc and transition rules of FRPNs respectively. According to the transition relation and monitoring logic, stateflow-based simulating model of FRPNs was constructed by use of above elements. Fired by control chart data, the model can analyze the occurrence degree of abnormity pattern in control chart, show the diagnosis process dynamically and finally give the diagnosis result. The result illustrated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Combination of two Shewhart-type control charts to detect small as well as large shifts in multivariate process variability
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper proposes a procedure based on two Shewhart-type control charts for monitoring the stability of multivariate process variability. That procedure will be able to detect small shift as well as large shift in covariance structure. For that purpose, generalized variance and vector variance will be used as multivariate variability measures. If generalized variance chart is sensitive to the large shift, we show that vector variance chart is sensitive to the small shift. A real industrial example will be presented to illustrate the advantage of the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: The certificate of ISO 9001 toward improving the quality of small/medium industries in Iran
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Nowadays the usage of modern techniques of management has become an important necessity for economical and industrial units. Quality management as the most important and comprehensive method can assist the systems in providing products and services with better quality and fewer expenses. So as the result the necessity of standard application has become appeared so important by industries. Today the importance of the quality orientation and its position has been a dominated vision in most organizations and their communications. Quality management has been founded as a necessity toward the organization's survive and its existance. There has been a significant growth for applying the quality management system because of auditing process and issuing its related certificates. This study is chasing to configure the benefits and advantages of ISO 9001 standard certificate and its important roles in the organization's performance. In this study 120 small - medium enterprises (SMEs) in Isfahan have been selected as the society sample through the descriptive method. The data analysis declared that there is a positive significant relationship for applying the certificate of ISO 9001 and some factories as the organizational performance in organizations, organizational benefits, TQC.

articleTitle: The role of failure mode and effect analysis in verifying the purpose of knowledge management
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Development of various techniques sin new century quickly, the speed of innovation creation, progress of efficiency as a result of two previous factor emphasis in this two issues that organizations and structures should control their systematic and management deficiencies by a concentrated system and by knowledge from outside to inside of the organization, so that they can continue their works in the field of competition with others. In the field of services and production activity issues like intensity, competition and raising of expectance and evolutions of technology cause raising of producer's commitment in the field of removing production's defects and wiping out any kinds of defects and deviation in performance. In this research, one of the quality management's techniques Failure mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) is considered as a systematic way for identifying and avoiding the occurrence of the problems so that optimize the process and production and in turn this cause decrease in the cost and then the purpose of knowledge management has been met.

articleTitle: An efficient approach of multi response optimization in Taguchi method (A case study on Gasoline production of Isfahan oil refining company)
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: In this paper, an attempt has been made to present an efficient approach for multi response optimization in Taguchi method. In this approach, best weight for each response is achieved by objectives that ensure maximization of both weighted normalized S/N ratios (WNSN) and minimum weighted SN ratios in each treatment. Using a sensible weight calculation to highlight treatments which have important role in total aggregation of WNSN and highest minimum value of WNSN among others is a important point in this paper, whereas In the prior studies, weights of SN ratio for each response are determined achieving the maximum weighted SN ratio that do not consider WNSN deviations. For this purpose, weight calculation model, the regression analysis and analysis of variance (ANOVA) are used to compute the weights, predict the relation model and clarify the effective terms, respectively. Finally, a case study for optimizing Gasoline production process is surveyed and results show improvement in real experiments.

articleTitle: Storage reliability evaluation of engine control circuit module
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The traditional method of storage reliability evaluation is based on the statistical analysis by numerous test data. This method is not suitable for practical engineering analysis due to the characteristic of its short development cycle and application period for the whole system. In this paper, method of storage reliability evaluation combing similar products method and test method is introduced. By analyzing the failure mechanism of engine control circuit module, use both similar products and test method to evaluate reliability of various types of failure. Then, evaluate the storage reliability of engine control circuit module by the use of system key components reliability series-parallel model.

articleTitle: A Markov-based control chart for dependent binary data
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: There are different statistical approaches for monitoring proportion when the observations are binary. Usually, it is considered that the data are independent. But there are situations in which the data are intrinsically correlated. In this paper, two Markov-based charts, the Markov EWMA and the Markov Shewhart, are presented as reasonable charts for dependent binary observations and a new method named Markov CUSUM chart is developed. It is shown that the one-sided Markov CUSUM chart has better performance than the two other charts in most situations by calculating ARL values. However, the significant extension of this paper over past works is in providing an effective first-order Markov model for dependent data based on individual binary observations.

articleTitle: Reliability estimation in heavy-tailed distributions using a robust estimator
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Heavy-tailed distributions have wide applications in life-time contexts, especially in reliability and risk modeling. So we consider the estimation problem of reliability, R = P(X >; Y), when X and Y are two independent but not identically distributed random variables belonging to the family of heavy-tailed distributions, using a robust estimator, namely the harmonic moment estimator. Extensive simulation studies are carried out to study the performance of this estimator.

articleTitle: The solutions of DT and AHP for supplier selection problem
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: In real-life situations, supplier selection problems involve multiple selection criteria and the risk associated with supplier failure. It is a fact that the best solution is to develop a solution methodology that combines these two decision factors simultaneously. The literature proposes the analytic hierarchical process (AHP) as a solution to multiple selection criteria problem. On the other hand, the decision tree (DT) can deal with the risk associate with supplier failure problem. This paper is an attempt to investigate the possibility that the results obtained separately from applying DT and AHP to supplier selection problem could help the decision maker to overcome the weakness inherited in each model.

articleTitle: Knowledge management practices in supply chain: A sectorial analysis
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The main aim of this paper is to investigate the similarities in knowledge management (KM) practices in supply chain (SC) among different selected sectors of Indian manufacturing organizations through formulation and testing of some hypotheses. A questionnaire-based survey was conducted on four sectors namely Automobile (Auto), Engineering, Process and FMCG (Fast Moving Consumer Goods). The findings of the sectorial analysis show that selected sectors do not significantly differ on use of various channels in managing the explicit knowledge of SC, use of KM in improving SC efficiency and its SC effectiveness.

articleTitle: Innovative Six-Sigma application by using the Quality Function development for mobile device compliance
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The practical method in Six-Sigma is introduced in the paper. The alternative application of Quality Function Deployment is applied for revealing the relationship between test cases and requirements of a mobile phone and it is an innovative approach for mobile phone compliant analysis for the mobile requirements. The set of test cases is a practical tool for evaluation of mobile phone quality for both carriers and vendors. Tractable results are obtained by using a linear algebra and matrix calculus that enable us to determine the optimized set of test cases.

articleTitle: Job involvement, job satisfaction, and organizational commitment: Predicting propensity to leave a job among skilled employee
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper examines the impact of job involvement, job satisfaction and organizational commitment on propensity to leave a job. Using a stratified random sampling procedure, survey questionnaires are administered to 116 Information Systems (IS) personnel working in multinational companies in Malaysia. Results show that IS personnel's job involvement is positively associated with organizational commitment. Likewise, job satisfaction has a positive relationship on organizational commitment. Employees' organizational commitment also significantly influences their propensity to leave a job. The findings of this study are discussed in the light of previous evidence. This paper concludes with a discussion of implications and directions for future studies for IS research.

articleTitle: On the impulsive Beverton-Holt equation and extinction conditions in population dynamics
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper is devoted to investigate extinction and non-extinction conditions of the extended Beverton-Holt equation for dynamics of populations in Ecology when potential discontinuities at sampling points are included in the model. Such discontinuities are related to impulses in the corresponding continuous-time logistic equation. The discontinuities are parameterized by two sequences of parameters, namely, the harvesting (i.e. the hunting or fishing quota) and the internal consumption which can include positive and negative migrations in the considered population habitat.

articleTitle: Multiple objective system reliability post-Pareto optimality using self organizing trees
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Multiple objective system reliability optimization problems have been become more popular in engineering and have been deeply covered in literature. There are different approaches to address multiple objective optimization problems depending of the area and special characteristics of the problem. Most of the methods developed to solve these types of problems consist in a Pareto set of optimal solutions. At this point the decision-maker has to select one solution among the Pareto set. This task is not trivial due to the large size of the set to choose for. This work presents a new method based on self-organizing trees for reducing the size of Pareto-optimal sets. The method is tested in several Pareto sets from different multiple objective system reliability optimization problems including a network reliability design problem.

articleTitle: Change point estimation in multi-attribute processes
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Identification of the change point in multi-attribute processes make the corrective measures to be employed sooner. This of course results in considerable amount of time and money savings. In real-world problems, since most of the process changes are due to instantaneous causes (step-change), a new method is proposed in this paper to derive the maximum likelihood estimator of the time of a step-change in the mean vector of multi-attribute processes. The results of a performance study based on a numerical example are encouraging.

articleTitle: Approximation and quantiles of the distribution of the modified likelihood ratio criteria for covariance matrix testing and monitoring
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Sugiura [11] gives an asymptotic expansion of the modified likelihood ratio criteria for testing the hypothesis that a covariance matrix is equal to a given matrix. An improvement of this expansion is presented here. Numerical comparisons via simulation with the original approximation to the criteria's distribution confirm the superiority of our expansion. This enable us to use the proposed method in usual hypotheses testing and in applications where extreme tail quantiles are necessary, as for instance, for monitoring dispersion in multivariate processes quality control charts.

articleTitle: Exploring business excellence in Asia
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper explores the use of Business excellence (BE) within Asian organisations. The paper observes the relative effectiveness of BE in Asian organisations as well as the organisations' attitudes towards BE awards. 74 organisations from five Asian countries were surveyed and 21 discussion groups were also conducted in all five countries. 13 interviews were also held with senior executives of BE award winning organisations. The study found that Asian organisations found BE to be important in helping them reach their organisational goals (both short and long term). However, there are several barriers to long-term commitment to BE within Asia; these include deficiencies in the development of a BE culture and a lack of comprehensive training programmes to fully educate staff in BE.

articleTitle: Cost of quality model development, verification and validation
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Undoubtedly simulation can help managers to enhance their decisions since it provide an opportunity to understand complex systems. In the case of quality control activities, simulation can be used to assist quality control managers to determine the cost involved to implement a specific quality control policy. Having said all that, one of the most challenging problems faced by the simulation modelling developer is the verification and validation aspects. This paper considers the model developed by [1] and explains a solution methodology carried by the authors to deal with the verification and validation aspects of the developed simulation model.

articleTitle: A replacement policy for a cold standby system with dependent lifetime and repair time
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: In this paper we consider a cold standby system having two units with a single repair facility. The reward and the repair cost per unit time depend on the number of times a unit has been repaired. Also it is assumed that some extra amount has to be paid for restarting the system after each down time. The replacement policy considered here is to replace the system upon the N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> failure of the first unit. A general expression for long-run expected cost per unit time is derived. An explicit expression of the cost function is derived by assuming that the joint distribution of the lifetime of a unit and the repair time of the other unit has Freund [1] bivariate exponential distribution. Existence of optimum value of N that minimizes the long-run expected cost per unit time is examined analytically and a numerical example is considered for illustration.

articleTitle: Local firms' knowledge acquisition in developing countries: Synergy between relationship embeddedness and absorptive capacity
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Global manufacturing network provides local firms in developing countries an important opportunity to acquire knowledge and innovate technologically. In the open innovation environment, different types of local firms participating in global manufacturing network have different performance in synergy between relationship embeddedness and absorptive capacity, which lead to its internal logic complexity of knowledge acquisition and uncertainty of innovative evolution path. Thus, this study theoretically discusses the different paths of knowledge acquisition for different local firms in developing countries respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of an out-of-control signals in process variability monitoring using network topology approach
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Identifying the root causes of an out-of-control signal is a crucial part in statistical process control. In this paper we propose a network topology approach to do such analysis in multivariate process variability monitoring. A real example will be presented to illustrate the analysis of the proposed method.

articleTitle: ESSQ management integration in international industrial companies
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The sectors of ESSQ management, namely the environment, safety & security and quality, have become increasingly important targets of development in companies in the prevailing global competition. The development of management systems, as well as the consideration of ESSQ matters and integrating them under the same system, has become an important factor of competitiveness. When observing management from the perspective of a systems approach, one of the focal elements is a common holistic management system of the company, to which ESSQ matters and other critical factors for success are thematically linked.

articleTitle: Design of data communication protocol in software test system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Simulation system is a real time system, in which data communication mechanism is the key point to assure the correctness of test data and real time data transferring. This paper will start from the architecture of simulation test system, and then build a data communication model according to data type and transferring requirements of the simulation test system. We present a test data communication mechanism based on data communication model. We elaborate the design of architecture of the communication mechanism and the design of software protocol.

articleTitle: Ecological cost accounting applied to the sewage reuse by membrane separation process
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The aim of the present study was to obtain the water of reuse from domestic sewage provided by Anhumas Sewage Treatment Station, from Campinas, Brazil. The construction building waste was used in decantation of sludge from sewage. The sewage water was filtered in a membrane of microfiltration and used in irrigation. Bean seeds are used in germination on degraded soils. Ecological cost was measured. Results showed that the membrane separation process demonstrated that is a method very efficiently in the removal of chemical parameters from sewage, what made its reuse. Of accordance to ECA results, the saving with the water of reuse produced in this work; was of US$ 13 million. It is demonstrated that this technology is ecologically and economically viable.

articleTitle: Design of inspection plans for a Stainless Steel Furniture Factory
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This research investigates the inspection process of a Stainless Steel Furniture Factory. There are an increasing number of customer complaints due to lack of standard and inconsistency of inspection, especially for the key processes. The new inspection plans are designed for those processes to overcome this issue. Based on Military Standard 105E (MIL-STD-105E), two acceptance sampling plans are proposed using the single sampling plan at AQLs 1.0 and 1.5. However, the inspection results are verified by 100% inspection with respect to their reliability and inspection time and cost. In conclusion, the acceptance sampling plan at AQL 1.0 is selected for cutting, drilling, and welding processes while the 100% inspection is used for chemical, assembly and finishing processes because of small lot size and vital processes. This approach can ensure that only good quality products will be delivered to the customer and the result shows that the customer complaints has decreased by 51.69%.

articleTitle: Efficiently estimating mean shift due to variability
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper concerns the problem of calculating expectation shift due to variability which tends to occur whenever the function of a random variable is nonlinear and especially tends to occur in the neighborhood of a local maximum or minimum. The paper presents five theorems suggesting sampling points and formulae for estimating mean shift covering some of the most common cases of practical interest including multivariate normal distributions and uniform distributions as well as more general theorems covering all symmetric multivariate probability density functions.

articleTitle: Improving reliability by modifying system configuration
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: This paper investigates how to improve system reliability by modifying the configuration of its components to realize a robust design. The methodology is applied on the voltage regulator of an electronic circuit with a +5volts regulated power supply. The effect of three different design modifications on the overall system reliability has been investigated, series redundancy, parallel redundancy and parallel-series redundancy. A single factor linear regression with median rank model is used to evaluate the reliability of the three suggested designs. The inverse power law model is used to characterize the relationship between system lifetime (L) and stress (voltage) level (V). Parallel-series design showed the best results regarding system reliability. The average Time-to-Failure at 25 volts stress level for the parallel-series design was found to be 3.5 times that of the initial design, 2.5 times that of the series design and 2.17 times that of the parallel design.

articleTitle: MCEWMA control chart to detect small shift for autocorrelated water treatment process responses
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Statistical process control (SPC) chart for individual observation helps to understand the state of control, stability, and capability of a process. However, most of the typical control chart suggested for individual observation is primarily based on the assumption that the process data are independent and normally distributed. This assumption of independency and normality is generally violated in many chemical processes. Response characteristic or output may have autocorrelation (or data are time dependent), and traditional control chart becomes practically unsuitable for such situations. A two-stage time series modelling and monitoring of residual approach by using control chart or using variable control limit-based MCEWMA is generally recommended. These charts can detect small shift for autocorrelated individual responses. In this paper, the usefulness of MCEWMA chart to detect small shift for autocorrelated mineral water treatment process is verified. The ARL values for MCEWMA are also proposed based on simulation results. The case study results confirms the suitability of ECWMA and is recommended as an alternative to the two-stage time series model and residual special control chart approach.

articleTitle: Warranty logistics issues in auto engine industry
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Warranty logistics deals with various issues relating to the servicing of warranty. Proper management of warranty logistics is needed not only to reduce the warranty servicing cost but also to avoid customer dissatisfaction since it has a negative impact on sales and revenue. Controls should be instituted to minimize the total cost of logistics rather than minimizing each component of the total cost. Warranty logistics mainly deals with the transportation of spares, warehousing, and warranty claims settlement and reverse logistics of the failed components. This paper illustrates a real life case study of an automobile engine manufacturer. There are two players; one of them is an engine manufacturer who supplies these engines to an automobile OEM. Various issues involved in forward and reverse logistics of the spare parts and failed components respectively have been studied. Issues faced by manufacture are discussed and solutions to overcome these problems are suggested.

articleTitle: How to measure the discrimination between two lifetimes in a time interval
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Measure of uncertainty about predictability of failure time of a system at the interval of time has been introduced in [13]. In this paper, a measure of discrepancy between two lifetime distributions at the interval of time is proposed on the basis of Kullback-Leibler discrimination information. We study the Kullback-Leibler measure for two-sided truncated random variables. We study various properties of this measure, including its connection with residual and past measures of discrepancy, and we obtain its upper and lower bounds.

articleTitle: A modified age reduction PM model in a finite time span
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: For an age reduction preventive maintenance (PM) model over a finite time span (L), it is found from literature that a shorter interval between each PM (T) can result in a better expected total maintenance cost (TC). The optimal policy of the stated PM model (called the original PM model) is usually obtained by searching the optimal value of T over the specified range (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub>, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>) for a given number of PM (N) by minimizing the total maintenance cost where T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub> and T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub> are defined as L/(N+1) and L/N, respectively. However, the original PM model does limit the possibility of finding a smaller TC since the value of T is constrained in the range of (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub>, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>). In this paper, we consider the idea of releasing the constraint of the searching range of T and propose a new PM model with age reduction in a finite time period which can have a better optimal solution than the corresponding original PM model. The algorithm of finding the optimal solution for the new model is developed. Examples of the proposed new model are provided and are compared with the corresponding original PM model.

articleTitle: The uncertainty of preventive maintenance cycle time of machinery based on cost — Revenue ratio model
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Determining the optimal preventive maintenance cycle time is one of the problems in maintenance task because there are many factors to be considered such as continuous operation, equipment conditions or the necessity of delivery date. Theoretically, preventive maintenance (PM) cycle time is inconsistent and it is assumed as normal distribution or N(MTTF,σ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The assumption in this paper considers the relationship between the cost of monitoring and the extra revenue when the machine operation is still in good conditions during the PM interval. On the other hand, if the machine operation fails before PM interval, there are the opportunity lost costs due to lack of manufactured parts and cost of failure to be considered. This paper presents the developed model for the relationship between the uncertainty of PM interval and cost - revenue ratio. The mathematical model in this paper is φ(δ*/σ)/Φ(δ*/σ)=C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sub>σ/R-(L+C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>). At the conclusion, the developed model is validated by using published data from previous research.

articleTitle: A modified Monte Carlo EM algorithm for a three-parameter distribution
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Statistical inference of a three-parameter distribution with closed-form mean residual life function is studied for complete and Type-II censored data. Because the log-likelihood function for this new distribution is not convex, the sequential quadratic programming method used for the maximum likelihood estimation easily diverges. Therefore, a modified Monte Carlo EM algorithm is proposed for parameter estimation. This modified algorithm is used to maintain the feasibility of the parameter vector during the evolutionary process, and is found to be robust in the sense that it is insensitive to the starting points.

articleTitle: Research on risk management gains of construction project based on the goal orientation perspective
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: On the basis of full access to risk cost related literature, find that the concept of risk management gains doesn't get closely enough with engineering practice in reality. Stat from the hierarchical structure of project contract system on, put forward the management idea of risk management and goal management integration. Constructed the equilibrium analysis methods of risk management gains by engineering project goal oriented, which composed of qualitative analysis, quantitative analysis and marginal analysis, further discusses the risk management gains equilibrium analysis process and the decision-making process. Provide scientific decision support for risk management to meet the need of project target management and help project parties realize the balance of gains and risks.

articleTitle: Nonparametric estimation of survival function in the presence of information through functionals
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: We are motivated by the reference [5] on nonparametric maximum likelihood estimate (NPMLE) of a lifetime cumulative distribution function (cdf) F on the basis of two independent samples, one of size m from F and the second of size n from G(x), a length biased distribution of F. One can obtain NPMLE of S(x) = 1 - F(x), the Survival Function when G is a suitable functional of F. We obtain NPMLE of 5, when G(t) is known a positive power of F. When power is unknown we propose estimators of the power and F. Based on extensive simulations, performance of estimators, using sup, L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> norms have been studied.

articleTitle: A step-by-step model to improve delivery assurance: A case study in mining industry
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Achieving a high level of Delivery Assurance is critical, but a difficult task for plant managers and engineers on site. In this paper, a step-by-step model was proposed to help making decisions for improving delivery assurance. After introducing the model in the second part, steps were discussed with general “inputs”, “methods & techniques” and “outputs”, separately. Besides, a case study was shown in the fourth part, to demonstrate its use in mining industry.

articleTitle: Maintenance metrics: A hierarchical model of balanced scorecard
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: The system of performance measurement of maintenance function should cover all processes related to it within the organization. There must be an interconnection between the different indicators, so the numbers can be interpreted in order to reach a good conclusion for decision making. This premise implies a hierarchy of indicators needed in a dual way. First, it will require maintenance indicators to be segmented according to the areas of influence for the rest of the organization, posed by interactions with finance department, human resources, purchasing, and, of course, with production in the seeking of compliance with corporate objectives. Simultaneously, these indicators correspond to different levels in the organization and therefore they will be segmented according to the hierarchical position of end users.

articleTitle: Integration of Six Sigma with a QMS based on the ISO 9001 requirements: A Portuguese SME case study
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: Organizations around the world are increasingly striving to adopt internal management systems and continuous improvement strategies to be able to compete in the global marketplace. In this context, Six Sigma and ISO 9001 quality management systems (QMS) are two well-known and popular approaches. Although their scopes diverge, there are many potential beneficial synergies between them, which can be useful for companies to take advantage of. By exploiting the relationships between Six Sigma and QMS based on the ISO 9001 standard, this paper proposes ways to integrate them attending to the structure and common elements of the ISO Guide 72.

articleTitle: A decision model for selecting of areas for improvement in EFQM model
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Quality and Reliability
abstract: To monitor the progress towards business excellence, thousands of organizations across the world use self-assessment on a regular basis. There are a few popular business excellence models that provide standard criteria against which an organization can measure its performances. European Foundation for Quality Management (EFQM) is the most popular ones. The EFQM Excellence Model was introduced at the beginning of 1992 as the framework for assessing organizations for the European Quality Award. It is now the most widely used organizational framework in Europe and across the world and it has become the basis for the majority of international, national and regional Quality Awards. It is a practical tool that can be used as a guide to identify areas for Improvement. However, the current EFQM model has some drawbacks and problems which are not able to identify the priorities in Area for Improvement (AFI). For organizations with limitations of time, budget and resources and cannot implement all the Area for Improvement, some standards or indexes and limitations should be defined for prioritizing and choosing the Area for Improvement. Using Topsis<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> method which is one of the multi-attribute decision making model, the Area for Improvement can be identified. Therefore, this work will develop a method of evaluating, assessing and determining the Area for Improvement in the EFQM model. The results showed that the developed model is more valid and acceptable and the experts verified the model for selecting of Area for Improvement in EFQM in practice. The proposed model was employed in a case study and drawn out results from it and were evaluated from different points of view.
